BLOG_POSTS.title: How to Make Layered Resin Coasters
BLOG_POSTS.excerpt: Get that trendy ocean-wave look with simple pouring and tilting techniques.
BLOG_POSTS.content:
Layered resin coasters are one of the most popular beginner resin projects, and the technique is simpler than it looks...

Start by mixing your casting resin in small batches, tinting each with a drop of mica pigment. Pour your first layer into the mold and let it set to a tacky stage before adding the next. Tilt the mold gently between layers to create natural, wave-like blending at the color boundaries. Once fully cured, sand the edges and buff with a polishing compound for a glass-like shine.

BLOG_POSTS.title: Beginner's Guide to Soy Candle Making
BLOG_POSTS.excerpt: The exact temperatures, ratios, and wick sizes for your first pour.
BLOG_POSTS.content:
Soy wax is the most forgiving wax for first-time candle makers. In this guide we'll walk through choosing the right wick size for your container diameter, melting temperatures, and how to add fragrance oil at the right stage for maximum scent throw...

As a general rule, use about 1oz of fragrance oil per pound of wax, added once the melted wax cools to around 175°F. Pour at 135°F and let cure for at least 48 hours before burning for the best scent throw.

BLOG_POSTS.title: Cold Process Soap 101: Working Safely with Lye
BLOG_POSTS.excerpt: Everything a first-timer needs to know before mixing their first batch.
BLOG_POSTS.content:
Lye (sodium hydroxide) is what turns oils into soap through saponification, and while it sounds intimidating, it's completely safe when handled correctly...

Always add lye to water — never water to lye — to avoid a volcanic reaction. Wear gloves and eye protection, work in a ventilated space, and use a dedicated digital scale for accuracy. Once mixed into soap and fully cured, no free lye remains in the finished bars.

BLOG_POSTS.title: 5 Concrete Planter Ideas for Your Patio
BLOG_POSTS.excerpt: Simple pours that look like a designer store bought them.
BLOG_POSTS.content:
Concrete planters have a modern, textural look that's surprisingly easy to achieve at home with a craft-grade mix...

Try nesting two molds of different sizes to create a raised-edge planter, or mix in iron-oxide pigment for a warm terracotta tone. A light sanding after curing gives a smooth, matte-store-bought finish.
